metadata.file_name: 110. Ang et al. (2020). Big Educational Data & Analytics: Survey, Architecture and Challenges.pdf
metadata.title: Big Educational Data & Analytics: Survey, Architecture and Challenges

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This article is a comprehensive literature review of big educational data sources, architectures, and analytics approaches, rather than an empirical analysis of ILSA microdata. As such, it does not define an assessment sampling frame, student-level analytic sample, or any survey-weight variables (e.g., TOTWGT, W_FSTUWT) for population-representative estimation. The review discusses predictive analytics and learning analytics methods in general, but it does not report how any complex survey design would be handled for achievement scaling or plausible-value estimation. Therefore, no weight variable can be specified for replication; any future empirical study using ILSA microdata should apply the official ILSA student weights and replicate weights (if provided) when estimating population-representative effects.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this paper does not conduct an empirical ILSA-style achievement analysis with PV-based dependent variables. Instead, it synthesizes prior work on big educational data sources and analytics paradigms, including predictive analytics and learning analytics, without estimating PV-based achievement scores from an ILSA dataset. As a result, there is no PV generation/combining or PV-specific missing-data strategy to document.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No ILSA/NAEP/CEDRE/INVALSI microdata analytic sample is constructed. The paper is a narrative literature review and includes illustrative examples (e.g., cross-institution web scraping in Australia) but does not define a student assessment sample with inclusion/exclusion criteria comparable to large-scale assessment microdata.

main_findings.dataset_used: ILSA literature synthesis (systematic review; no single student-level analytic micro-dataset)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ILSA literature synthesis (systematic review; no single student-level analytic micro-dataset) the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Literature synthesis outcome (not student-level prediction), finding that This paper is a review article that synthesizes the landscape of big educational data and analytics, covering data sources (e.g., LMS, MOOC, OER, social media, linked data, mobile learning), data collection approaches (e.g., xAPI), and technological architectures (e.g., Hadoop, Spark, Samza). It organizes analytics approaches into predictive analytics, learning analytics (collaborative/interactive, behavioral, personalized, social/network-based, and assessment analytics), recommendation systems, graph analytics, visual analytics, social media analytics, and immersive learning analytics. While it mentions performance metrics from cited studies (e.g., accuracy, AUC, MAP) and provides an illustrative cross-institution graph-analytics scenario using web scraping and Bag of Words features, it does not estimate a unified predictive model on a single ILSA-style dataset. Consequently, there are no PV-based achievement benchmarks, no ILSA sampling/weighting scheme, and no single set of effect sizes attributable to this paper itself. The main contribution is conceptual and methodological synthesis rather than empirical causal or predictive estimation. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: Because this is a review article, it does not report an original student-level dataset, PV handling, missing-data handling, or a single ML training/evaluation pipeline. The absence of sample sizes, country-level Ns, and model performance metrics is expected for a synthesis paper that aggregates findings from heterogeneous prior studies and illustrative examples rather than conducting one coherent large-scale assessment analysis.
